h1: The 8 Best Roomba Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Roomba Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 iRobot Roomba robot vacuums scored on dock type, mopping and suction, from the 105 Vac to the Plus 505 Combo and 415X.
summary: The Roomba Plus 505 Combo is the Roomba to buy: LiDAR mapping, extending spinning mop pads and a dock that washes and heat-dries them. If you want a dock-free setup, the 205 DustCompactor goes up to 60 days between emptying. For pet owners, the Max 705 uses rubber brushes that resist tangles. On a budget, the 105 Vac gives LiDAR mapping at the lowest cost of the range.
intro: Roomba shoppers face an odd problem: the range has four model families, a dozen suffixes, and similar names that hide very different hardware. A 105 and a 105 Combo are not the same machine, and a 405 is not a 505 with a different sticker.

We reviewed eight current Roombas and ranked them by what the hardware actually does, mainly the dock, the mop system and the brush design. Scores follow the Primea framework. We paid close attention to what you give up at each step down the range.

products.name: iRobot Roomba Plus 505 Combo Robot Vacuum and Mop with AutoWash Dock
products.verdict: Extending spinning mop pads, an AutoWash Dock that heat-dries them and LiDAR mapping.
products.description:
The Plus 505 Combo pairs vacuuming with extending, spinning mop pads and a dock that rinses the pads and dries them with heat after each run, so nobody has to handle a soiled pad. LiDAR plans each room in turn, and the same dock empties the bin.

It wins because it automates mopping, the chore most robots still leave to you. The 415X outdoes it on suction and dock life, but costs more. Against the cheaper Plus 405, you pay for the extending mop and a more polished system.

Best for hard-floor homes that want mopping handled start to finish.
pros: Dock washes and dries mop pads
products.idealFor: Hard-floor homes wanting mopping fully automated.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 415X Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo
products.verdict: 2.3X suction, a 90-day self-emptying dock and hot-dry mop cleaning. The top of the range.
products.description:
The Roomba 415X is the most expensive model in the guide, centered on 2.3X suction, a dock that empties the robot for up to 90 days and cleans and hot-dries the mop pads. It also steers around obstacles intelligently.

It ranks second only because of price. For a large home or a household that wants the longest stretch between touching the dock, it is the better machine than the 505 Combo. For a typical home, the 505 offers most of the benefit for less.

Best for large homes and anyone who wants the fewest chores.
products.skipIf: Your home is small or your budget is tight.

products.name: iRobot Roomba Plus 405 2in1 Vacuum and Mop Robot with AutoWash Dock
products.verdict: Dual spinning mop pads and the AutoWash Dock at a lower price than the 505.
products.description:
Costing clearly less than the 505 Combo, the Plus 405 still has the AutoWash Dock, twin spinning mop pads and quick mapping that lets it clean one room at a time. It is a true 2-in-1 rather than a vacuum with an add-on tank, so its mopping lands near the flagship's.

It ranks third because it lacks the extending mop arm and the other refinements of the 505. For most homes with ordinary baseboards, you will not miss them.

A good fit for buyers who want automatic mop washing and sensible pricing.
products.idealFor: Value-minded buyers wanting self-washing mop pads.
products.skipIf: You want the extending edge mop.

products.name: iRobot Roomba Max 705 Robot Vacuum with AutoEmpty Dock
products.verdict: Vacuum-only with powerful suction and dual rubber anti-tangle brushes.
products.description:
The Roomba Max 705 puts its effort into strong suction and twin rubber brushes that resist tangling, an iRobot habit that sets it apart from bristle-roller rivals. Rubber brushes are worth considering for long hair and pet fur, which tend to wrap around bristle rollers. LiDAR navigation and an AutoEmpty dock complete the setup.

It ranks fourth because it does not mop. If your home is carpeted, or you already own a mop, that is no loss and the money goes into suction and brush design.

Best for carpeted homes with long-haired people or shedding pets.
products.idealFor: Carpeted homes with pets or long hair.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 205 DustCompactor Vac Robot Vacuum
products.verdict: Compacts dirt inside the robot for up to 60 days between emptying. No dock to house.
products.description:
The Roomba 205 DustCompactor takes a different approach from the rest of the range: instead of a self-emptying dock it squeezes dirt down inside the robot, so you open the bin only about every 60 days. Nothing bulky sits on your floor, just a small charging base. It is bagless.

It ranks fifth because it is not as hands-off as the docked models, and you still touch the bin every couple of months. But for a small flat where a dock does not fit, it solves the real problem.

Pick it for apartments and studios with limited floor space.
pros: No dock to find room for

products.name: iRobot Roomba 105X Robot Vacuum
products.verdict: 70X power-lifting suction, smart mapping and custom room cleaning from the app.
products.description:
Step up from the base 105 Vac and you reach the 105X, with 70X power-lifting suction and room-specific cleaning in the iRobot Home app, where maps, no-go zones and schedules live. App and voice control are both included.

Some functions, like a no-go zone or a room-specific schedule, live in the app, so you will rely on your phone. It ranks sixth because it has no dock, so the step up from the base model is mostly suction and control.

A good middle step for buyers who want better suction without a docked price.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting stronger suction and room control.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 105 Combo Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: Basic mopping on the entry platform, with LiDAR that detects carpet and avoids it.
products.description:
The Roomba 105 Combo takes the entry 105 and gives it simple mopping. Its LiDAR spots carpet and skips it, so a wet pad never crosses your rugs. There is no AutoWash Dock, so you rinse and reattach the mop pad by hand.

It ranks seventh because the Plus 405 gives automatic pad washing for not much more. For a small home with a few hard-floor rooms, the manual pad is acceptable.

Best for first-time mop buyers on a tight budget.
pros: Vacuum and mop on a budget
products.idealFor: First-time mop buyers with small hard-floor areas.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 105 Vac Robot Vacuum
products.verdict: Vacuum-only with LiDAR and power-lifting suction at the lowest cost of the range.
products.description:
The Roomba 105 Vac only vacuums: no mop pad, no water tank, no combo dock. It does keep LiDAR and power-lifting suction, which is more mapping than most budget robots offer.

It ranks last because everything else in the range adds something, whether a dock, mop or app control. For hard floors and low-pile carpets with light mess, it covers the basics and costs the least.

Choose it if you want neat-row cleaning from a name you know without paying for extras.
products.idealFor: Light-duty cleaning on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want a dock, mop or heavy-duty suction.

whatMatters.detail: A Roomba 105 Vac and a 105 Combo are different machines, and a Plus 405 is not a 505. Look for Combo or 2in1 in the title for mopping, and for dock names like AutoWash or AutoEmpty. Check the title word by word before ordering.
AutoWash docks wash and dry the mop pads between runs. Without one, you rinse the pad yourself, and a damp pad left on the robot can smell. If you mop weekly, AutoWash saves real effort.

A dock empties the robot into a bag, while the DustCompactor squeezes dirt inside the robot for up to 60 days. Docks suit larger homes, the compactor suits small spaces. Check which one the listing names.
Rubber brushes resist tangles from hair better than bristles. If anyone in your home has long hair or you have pets, look for rubber or anti-tangle in the specs.
A combo robot should avoid mopping carpet. The 105 Combo's LiDAR does so. Check the listing for carpet avoidance, or set no-go zones in the app.

faq.q: What is the difference between Roomba 105 models?
faq.a: The 105 Vac is vacuum-only, the 105 Combo adds basic mopping and the 105X adds 70X suction and app room cleaning. None has a self-emptying dock.

faq.q: Is the Plus 505 Combo worth more than the Plus 405?
faq.a: If you want the extending spinning mop, yes. Both have AutoWash Docks, so the 405 gives most of the benefit for less.
For no-go zones, room schedules and maps, yes, through the iRobot Home app. Basic cleaning can start with the robot's button.

faq.q: Will a Roomba mop my carpet?
faq.a: Combos like the 105 Combo detect carpet and avoid mopping it. For safety, also set no-go zones on rugs in the app.
It compacts dirt inside the robot, so you empty it only about every 60 days instead of using a dock. Bagless, so no bags to buy.

faq.q: Which Roomba is best for pet hair?
faq.a: The Max 705. Its dual rubber brushes resist tangling, and the AutoEmpty dock handles volume. For heavier loads the 415X adds stronger suction.

finalTake: For most homes the Roomba Plus 505 Combo is the right buy: LiDAR mapping, extending spinning mop pads and a dock that washes and dries them. For the least upkeep in a big house, the 415X empties for up to 90 days. For pets, the Max 705's rubber brushes avoid tangles. And for a tight budget, the 105 Vac covers the basics with LiDAR.
